# What Skills in Google Workspace Are and Who They Help

> **In short:** Google says skills in Google Workspace are reusable instructions that teach Gemini your team's rules, templates, and reference files. They are rolling out in Workspace Studio and Workspace apps, starting November 9, 2026 for Rapid Release domains and November 30, 2026 for Scheduled Release domains.

Have you ever explained the same email style or report format to an AI tool for the fifth time this month? Skills are Google's answer to that repetition. They let you write your preferred way of working once, then reuse it.

## What a skill actually is

A **skill** is a saved set of instructions. Think of it like a laminated checklist you hand to a new coworker: it says how things are done here, and the coworker follows it every time. In Google's announcement, a skill tells Gemini (Google's AI assistant) to follow your rules, use your templates, and check your reference files.

Skills are written in a format called **SKILL.md**, which is a plain text file with Markdown formatting. Markdown is just a light way of marking headings and lists with simple symbols. You don't need to know it to use skills, but it is useful to know that the format is open, so instructions can be copied between tools.

## Where you can use them

Google says you can create, test, and share skills in **Workspace Studio** (the place to build automated workflows) and **Google Docs**. You can also prompt Gemini directly in Gmail, Docs, Slides, Drive, and Chat to create and refine skills without leaving the app you are working in.

Once a skill is turned on, Gemini can recognize when it fits your request. You can also call one or more skills yourself by typing an @ followed by the skill's name. Skills can also start Workspace Studio flows set to "Start manually" or "On a schedule."

Some limits to know now: according to Google, skills are not yet available in Google Sheets or Google Meet, and they currently support English prompts and instructions only. Skills are also limited to users age 18 and older.

## What this means for you

- **For a team lead**: Write your brand voice or report format once, then share a copy with teammates. Sharing gives each person an independent copy, so your later edits won't overwrite theirs. If a skill points to Drive files, you'll need to share those files with them too.
- **For a sales or marketing specialist**: A skill can keep email drafts, proposals, and slides consistent with approved wording.
- **For an admin**: Google says skills are on by default for eligible editions, and you can turn them off at the domain, organizational unit, or group level in the Admin console. Audit log events are also available for monitoring skill activity.
- **If you're just getting started**: Open a skill-related file in Docs or ask Gemini in Gmail to help you draft one. Start small, with a single rule you repeat often.
- **If you already use it**: Combine two or more skills in one request with several @mentions, and point a skill at a Workspace Studio flow that runs on a schedule. Google notes that Gems in the Gemini app do not sync with skills built in Workspace, so you can copy instructions manually if you need them in both places.

## Wrap-up

Skills turn your team's habits into reusable instructions that Gemini can apply across Workspace. Google's announcement says rollout is gradual, so your feature may appear up to 15 days after your release date. Your next step is simple: check the Help Center articles Google links to, then write down one instruction you repeat every week and turn it into a skill.
